subject: MSA + Order Form: liability cap and IP indemnity carve-out (redlines attached)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: liability cap and IP indemnity carve-out (redlines attached)

Hi Elena / Daniel,

Thanks again for the productive call on Friday. Per our conversation, I've attached a redline of the MSA and the Order Form with the specific sections called out for the limitation of liability and indemnity. Key points for your legal team to review: 

- Redwood proposes a general liability cap equal to the fees paid by Acme in the 12 months preceding the claim (standard for our hosted plans).
- We have carved out indemnity obligations for IP infringement and for Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct (i.e., those obligations are not subject to the dollar cap).
- For IP indemnity specifically, our redline keeps defense obligations, provides for remediation (replacement/patch/credit), and requires that Redwood be given sole control of the defense where practicable.

For transparency: Acme asked during the call whether IP indemnity would be "unlimited." We understand why Acme would request that, but from Redwood's perspective we need a workable trade-off that keeps our commercial exposure bounded while still giving you a meaningful remedy for third-party IP claims. Our attached redline includes two alternative IP carve-out proposals (see section 10.2 in the doc):

A) Narrow carve-out: IP indemnity not subject to the monetary cap but limited to actual damages awarded by a court plus reasonable attorneys' fees and costs to defend, excluding punitive or exemplary damages. Redwood remains responsible for costs to obtain a replacement service in the event of an adverse judgment.

B) Broad carve-out: IP indemnity not subject to cap and includes damages, attorneys' fees, and amounts paid in settlements, but Redwood retains standard rights to control defense and to seek indemnitor contribution from third parties. This is what we would offer for enterprise accounts with an indemnity premium/commitment.

Please review the redline and let me know which of the two options (or another path) Acme prefers. If helpful, Rishi (cc'd) and Laura are on standby to coordinate the legal/finance trade-offs.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to narrow this down?

Best,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acmecloud.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: liability cap and IP indemnity carve-out (redlines attached)

Monica,

Thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. I circulated internally to our legal and procurement teams. A couple of initial points: 

- Acme's baseline position is that IP infringement indemnity should be uncapped (i.e., not subject to a monetary cap), and should include settlements and damages. Given the risk profile for our product integrations, we can't accept a cap that would leave us undercompensated for third-party claims.

- We are open to Redwood retaining control of defense, provided Acme has approval rights for any settlement that would impose restrictions or non-monetary obligations on Acme.

- Our procurement/legal team asked for an explicit statement that Acme's consequential damages are excluded (we still expect Redwood to cover IP indemnity and defense costs as carved out).

I've attached Acme's redline excerpt; you can see the requested uncapped language and a standard mutual waiver of consequential damages elsewhere. If Redwood insists on a cap for IP, we'd need to see evidence of insurance/backstop or higher cap multiples (e.g., 3x prior-year fees) plus an indemnity premium reflected in the Order Form.

Can Rishi and your legal team discuss the insurance/defense control questions? We're trying to avoid an extended back-and-forth, so a short call would help.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations | Acme Cloud
elena.ruiz@acmecloud.com | +1 650-555-0199

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: liability cap and IP indemnity carve-out (redlines attached)

Team,

Quick internal read on Acme's response and negotiating posture:

1) Uncapped IP indemnity is a significant exposure for Redwood if left unconstrained. However, Acme's ask is not unusual for larger customers. We need to balance commercial win vs. open-ended legal risk.

2) Recommended compromise (won't require special insurance initially):
   - Keep general liability cap = fees in prior 12 months.
   - Carve out IP indemnity from the cap, but expressly limit the remedy to: (i) amounts actually awarded by a court or paid in good-faith settlement; (ii) reasonable attorneys' fees and costs; and (iii) the reasonable cost to remediate or replace the infringing portion of the Service.
   - Exclude punitive, exemplary, and consequential damages from indemnity recovery (consistent with our commercial position), but allow Acme to seek injunctive relief without monetary cap.
   - Preserve Redwood's right to control the defense, but require Redwood to consult Acme and obtain consent for settlements that impose non-monetary obligations on Acme or a material payment beyond a threshold (suggest: $250k).

3) If Acme insists on a true "uncapped" settlement exposure (no monetary cap on IP indemnity), request either:
   - a contractual premium in the Order Form and a commitment to carry specific IP infringement insurance (we can source), or
   - a higher negotiated cap that scales with committed spend (e.g., 3x annual fees) for the term of the Order Form.

4) Draft language suggestion to send back (short form):
   "Notwithstanding the limitation of liability set forth above, each party's liability for claims under the indemnification provisions related to third-party claims of infringement of patents, copyrights, or trade secrets shall not be subject to the foregoing monetary cap; provided, however, that recovery shall be limited to (a) amounts finally awarded by a court or agreed in settlement, (b) reasonable costs and attorneys' fees incurred in connection with the defense, and (c) reasonable costs incurred to procure a non-infringing replacement or mitigation. Neither party shall be liable for punitive, special, or consequential damages under this Section. Redwood shall have the right to assume and control the defense, provided that Redwood shall not settle any claim that imposes injunctive relief or non-monetary obligations on Acme without Acme's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld."

5) Ask Laura to model the worst-case exposure numbers for a few contract sizes so we can see whether to flex pricing/insurance.

I'll tidy the suggested language and Monica can send to Acme as a formal counter.

-Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: liability cap and IP indemnity carve-out (redlines attached)

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the quick review and the clarity on Acme's position. We discussed internally and worked on a targeted compromise that we think preserves your ability to recover for third-party IP claims while keeping exposure commercially manageable for Redwood. Below is the redline-ready language we'd propose to insert in Section 10 (Limitation of Liability / Indemnity):

---Suggested contract language (for insertion into Section 10)---

"Notwithstanding any limitation of liability in this Agreement, Redwood's liability under the indemnification obligations for third-party claims alleging that the Service infringes a third party's intellectual property rights (IP Claim) shall not be subject to the foregoing monetary cap; provided, however, that recoverable amounts shall be limited to: (i) amounts finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or amounts paid in a good-faith settlement; (ii) reasonable and documented attorneys' fees and costs incurred in defending such IP Claim; and (iii) reasonable costs incurred to procure a non-infringing replacement or to modify the Service to avoid the IP Claim. The foregoing indemnity shall not include punitive, exemplary, or consequential damages. Redwood shall have the right to assume and control the defense of any IP Claim, provided that Redwood shall not settle or consent to entry of judgment that (A) imposes injunctive relief or other non-monetary obligations on Acme, or (B) requires payment by Acme in excess of $250,000, without Acme's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

In the event that Acme requires an uncapped monetary remedy for IP Claims, Redwood will discuss an indemnity premium to be reflected in the Order Form and the procurement of IP infringement insurance covering such exposure."

---end language---

We can present this language as our formal counter-proposal. Rishi will send a clean redline to incorporate this. If Acme prefers to keep the "uncapped" formulation, please let us know what specific insurance minimums or premium terms you'd expect so we can price accordingly.

Can we schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow at 10am PT to resolve remaining open points? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Monica
